categories.harassment: a person follows, blocks, touches, gropes, grabs or threatens another person who tries to move away or resist (stalking, eve-teasing, molestation)
categories.fighting: two or more people hit, kick, push or grapple with each other (assault, brawl)
categories.riot: a group acts violently: throwing stones or objects, damaging property, or clashing with police
categories.weapon: a person holds or uses a weapon such as a knife, gun, sword, or a stick or rod raised to strike
categories.fire: uncontrolled fire, flames or thick smoke, such as a burning vehicle, shop or building, also while firefighters or police work at it (not a stove, lamp, candle or cooking flame)
categories.arrest: police or officers (people in uniform) restrain, handcuff, hold the arms of, detain or escort a person who is being held. Officers who only stand, talk, work or direct traffic are not an arrest
categories.chase: one person or vehicle runs after or pursues another at speed
categories.person_down: a person has fallen or is lying on the ground and stays down
categories.accident: a road accident: vehicles collide, or a vehicle hits a person or overturns
categories.theft: a person snatches, grabs or takes someone's belongings and moves away quickly
categories.vandalism: a person deliberately breaks, damages or defaces property without a crowd clash
categories.crowd_incident: an area is dangerously overcrowded, or a crowd suddenly runs or scatters (stampede)
categories.tailgating: two or more people pass through an entrance one right behind the other
categories.suspicious_activity: a person lingers in one place for a long time, or a bag is left unattended
